- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match downward pressure.
- Model often underestimates sharp upward moves (especially after negative sentiment turns positive) — add a small upward bias to forecast if sentiment flips from negative to positive.
- Model frequently overestimates downward moves after positive sentiment — reduce forecast slightly if sentiment turns negative.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price peaks/troughs — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values if sentiment is volatile.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish — apply a small upward correction (e.g., +1–2% of range) in final 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.5.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) for 3+ days, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overreaction.
- Model tends to overshoot after spikes — if true price spikes > 5% from prior high, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
